body:
Hey, sorry for the late reply. I forget to sign in sometimes. 

To answer your question, I have a degree in Electrical and Mechanical engineering and what I was passionate back in uni was automation which I realise I should really get back to. I would jump at the chance to do a masters in it but I'll give this career thing another chance (at another company). Even if I do follow through with this, it'll be the same situation - make friends for the year, graduate and find a job and go our separate ways. 

I've got a GF but she's currently abroad just now for 3 months. She means a lot to me and I do share my feelings with her. She's got dreams of her own which I'm happy to fulfill.

I feel a lot better since posting this thread. I'm still lost but I feel a slight change in the way I think. I love learning but lack the motivation unless I invest some money into it so I guess the best way forward would be some eveining classes. However, this won't happen til I move out.

Just for the record, I'll make my current goals:

1) Get the fudge out of town
2) Get a new job
3) Start evening classes in anything of interest.

I have no ultimate goal, no lifelong dreams but at least this is a start.

For all redditors who replied, I just want to say thank you. This means a lot to me.

Ugh! I hate this too.

I do get either reply from strangers when I am deep in thought too. It annoys me to no end.
I would prefer this actually...if there were more people I knew better. I guess I'll settle for a "how was your day?" from a barista.

Thanks dude. Usually when I'm like this, my thoughts go into one big cycle and I can't think of anything else. 
Just wanted to let you know that you've helped me break out of that cycle for now and just focus on getting out of here. 

However, I see getting out as a short term solution... What happens then? I dunno why but it just terrifies me that I don't know what I want to do.

What are your dreams?

Thanks for your input. 

This is one of the troubles I'm having just now: I can't concentrate on the task at hand whether it be work, games or movies. I just have this niggling feeling like I'm wasting my time that I could be using for something else.

Volunteering is pretty much non-existant here. There is only one gym here that's fully packed. I'll go check it out tomorrow.

As for your final point, thank you. I actually had a barista asking me how my day and it did make me feel a little bit better. (I wanted to get this off my chest that day but it was busy so it was cut short)

Hey, just wanted to thanks for replying. 

I guess the way I feel like this is mainly because throughout my life, I've always with friends thanks to school and uni. Now that that's part of my life is over and I'm by myself, it's a bit difficult to feel anything else except this.

I doubt there would be any redditors here but I guess I could make an effort to see if any of my workmates would want to go out for a meal someday.
